# TradeJS Documentation

> Documentation for the TradeJS TypeScript framework: build, backtest, and run programmable trading strategies with a self-hosted runtime.

Docs home: https://docs.tradejs.dev
Russian docs: https://docs.tradejs.dev/ru/
Marketing site: https://tradejs.dev

## Start Here

For project work, read the project instructions and check installed package versions before choosing commands. Use the local backtest workflow for simulated tests and the MCP guide for access to a running app.

## MCP

TradeJS MCP connects Codex and Claude Code through OAuth and Streamable HTTP at /mcp. Read markets, charts, runtime strategies/signals/orders and verified evidence; run bounded cached backtest/diagnostic jobs through a separate worker. Requires a running MCP-enabled server and a server account. The local stable release 3.1.28 does not include MCP. No live order or deployment tools. Connection steps and example prompts: https://docs.tradejs.dev/guides/mcp (Russian: https://docs.tradejs.dev/ru/guides/mcp). The project owner can inspect data coverage, request gap downloads with market:backfill, and read saved studies with research:read.

Separately installed strategies outside Base: TradingPatterns (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/trading-patterns) VwapReversion (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/vwap-reversion), and RangeReclaim (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/range-reclaim). TradingPatterns supports 15-minute and hourly candles (hourly by default). LondonBreakout (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/london-breakout) and TrendPullback (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/trend-pullback) are also published separately.

Other standalone strategies:
- Crab (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/crab)
- Diamond (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/diamond)
- Triangle (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/triangle)
- ValueAreaReclaim (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/value-area-reclaim)
- ImbalanceMomentum (https://tradejs.dev/marketplace/imbalance-momentum)

## Automatic fixed-configuration research

Stable TradeJS includes research:core. Record the input data, costs, time boundaries and settings. Choose candidate rules on earlier data and evaluate on a later period. See https://docs.tradejs.dev/guides/develop-with-an-agent and https://docs.tradejs.dev/api/cli#automatic-strategy-research.

## Entry submission and replay diagnostics

Before entry submission, TradeJS checks Bybit’s quote and the final quantity; estimated loss above MAX_LOSS_VALUE produces a warning. Runtime debug also controls delivery of the verified live/replay comparison. See https://docs.tradejs.dev/runtime/execution/signals and https://docs.tradejs.dev/runtime/execution/telegram-notifications.

Mixed-timeframe replay evaluates each strategy on its own closed candles and can record the replay decision for an unmatched live entry. See https://docs.tradejs.dev/runtime/backtesting/replay-evidence.
